query: We just got paged: checkout is throwing 500s for most users and error rate is climbing. The last deploy went out 10 minutes ago. Run the incident.
expected_behavior: Confirms the impact with a signal (error-rate graph or a reproduced 500) and writes down surface, start time, and rough user count before acting
Declares a severity (SEV1) and names the criterion that set it (core flow down for most users)
Assigns a single named Incident Commander before diving into fixes
Mitigates first by the fastest reversible path (rolls back the 10-minute-old deploy or flips the feature flag) instead of root-causing the code live
Posts a first communication with impact, IC name, and a committed next-update time, keeping the internal channel separate from the external status page
Verifies recovery against the real signal over a hold window before declaring resolved, then drafts a blameless postmortem with a timeline and owned action items
